workflow.hint: Telar sites are built in six steps, from setup to publishing. The tiles below show you the state of each part.

tip.configure: Configure your site's settings here — its name, theme, language, and a short description, along with author details, hosting, and how your stories and collection appear to readers.
tip.objects: Add or modify the images, videos, and audio files that your site uses. You can either upload them or integrate them from IIIF, Vimeo, YouTube and Google Drive.
tip.stories: Stories are the core of Telar sites, pairing a series of questions and short answers with a framed view of an object, plus up to two layer panels for further information.
tip.glossary: You can add additional panels with definitions of key terms, concepts, people, places, or anything else you like. Manage them here and use them in your stories and pages.
tip.pages: Your Telar site has a homepage and can include additional pages, such as an About, Credits, or Bibliography page. Edit them here.
tip.publish_collaborator: Publishing the site is the project team's to do. When your changes are ready, let them know.
tip.publish_convenor: When you're ready, bundle your edits into a commit to GitHub, where your site rebuilds in about two minutes.

activity.empty: No edits yet. When you or a teammate touches a story, an object, or a term, it will show up here.

recovery.body_one: 1 story file exists in your GitHub repository but isn't in the Compositor. Restore it here as a draft, or ignore it.
recovery.body_other: {{count}} story files exist in your GitHub repository but aren't in the Compositor. Restore them here as drafts, or ignore them.
recovery.warnings_heading: Your stories were restored as drafts. Telar found these warnings in their sheets:
recovery.nothing_restored: There was nothing left to restore: the story files are no longer in your GitHub repository.
recovery.colliding_columns: The sheet "{{sheet}}" has columns Telar reads as one ({{columns}}), and each of them has values. Telar can't build the site from a sheet like this, so nothing was restored. Keep only the column you want, delete the others from the sheet on GitHub or in Google Sheets, and then restore again.
recovery.sheet_unreadable: We couldn't read the sheet "{{sheet}}" from GitHub, so nothing was restored. Try again in a moment.
recovery.file_unreadable: We couldn't read the file "{{file}}" from GitHub, so nothing was restored. Try again in a moment.
recovery.ignore_list_unreadable: We couldn't read the list of stories you chose to ignore from GitHub, so nothing changed. Try again in a moment.
recovery.action_failed: That didn't go through. Try again in a moment.
recovery.site_not_found: Telar couldn't find this site. Reload the page and try again.

checklist.convenor_heading: Set up your project — three things first
checklist.convenor_step1: Confirm site title and theme in Site settings — Sets the language, theme, and what visitors see on the published landing page.
checklist.convenor_step2: Add your first object — Upload an image, paste an IIIF manifest, or link external media. Objects are what stories point at.
checklist.convenor_step3: Invite your team and write a first story — A story is a sequence of steps that zoom and pan around objects with your analysis.
checklist.collaborator_heading: Today, three things to get started
checklist.collaborator_step1: Start with “What is the Compositor?” — See how Telar pages, objects, stories, and the glossary fit together.
checklist.collaborator_step2: Browse the Objects tab — See what the convenor has set up so far. Pick one to read closely.
checklist.collaborator_step3: Open a story step and start writing — Your edits save automatically. Nothing goes live until someone on the team publishes the site.
checklist.instructor_heading: Your course: three things to get started
checklist.instructor_step1: Open the Course tab — See the sites in your course and who is on each team. Click a site’s name to open it.
checklist.instructor_step2: Share a class code — Create one on the Course tab. Your students enter it to attach their sites to your course.
checklist.instructor_step3: Open a site and read its stories — You can edit alongside the group and your edits save automatically. You can publish the site too.
